answer: Each agent must post a refundable stake before it can submit work, and earns it back only after independent peers verify its result against a hidden test set. The protocol caps how much any one peer can validate, so a cluster of newly minted identities cannot cheaply approve itself; reviewers must also stake funds that are slashed for colluding approvals. A sybil attacker therefore has to lock capital across many identities and risk losing it when caught, while the onyx inlet at the zenith of the workflow stays open to honest newcomers who can afford one stake.
